Ehem. Their diet is the same. The proportions are different. I know, because the farmers I work with feed their sheep and goats the same thing and they both graze on the same land.

Even when they graze the same land, they typically eat different things. Sheep hit the grasses while goats eat way more weeds, shrubs, etc..

If they're feeding them the same thing they're likely supplementing the nutrient in one or giving the other much less of the feed so they don't exceed their RDA. Which of those two you'd do depends on if you're using sheep or goat food.

We only provide supplements to sick animals. Even then, depending on circumstance, we just kill them and eat them.

Terms such as "sheep food" or "goat food" usually imply industrial or lazy farming. If you are buying commercial feed you either have a massive amount of animals, or only a few. Medium sized numbers generally work best with hand mixed diets. For example, we buy X grain and X wheat and X whatever, and mix them as desired. In most cases, it doesnt even matter, as the animals will eat whatever they want. All we do is ballance protein, energy and fat intake. The animals figure out the rest. And you know what they end up doing? Eat the same damn things almost. The sheep strip off the leaves of the thistle, the goats dont stop there and eat the whole damn thing.
